conventions.convention: A 1-sub-Gaussian reward is integrable and satisfies E[exp(λ(X−E[X]))] ≤ exp(λ²/2) for every real λ.

All finite reward-table entries are mutually independent; learner randomness is independent of the entire table. Policies use only that randomness and previously revealed history; pulling an arm reveals its next unused stack entry.
Pseudo-regret is the random sum of mean gaps; realized reward regret is nμ* minus observed total reward; R_n denotes the expectation of realized reward regret.
UCB initializes every arm once, uses the natural-logarithm bonus sqrt(2 log(1/δ)/s), and chooses the least-index maximizer. The regret results set δ=n⁻².
Explore-then-commit requires positive integers m,k,n with mk≤n, explores round-robin, and commits to the least-index empirical-mean maximizer.

load_bearing.statement: The finite reward-stack model has mutually independent integrable entries with fixed arm laws, independent learner randomization, non-anticipating choices, and next-unused-entry rewards; gaps and both regret quantities are defined on that common probability space.
For q≥1 mutually independent integrable 1-sub-Gaussian real variables with means m_j, both tails of their centered sum at t≥0 are at most exp(−t²/(2q)).
For t∈[n], i∈[k], B∈H_{t−1} contained in {A_t=i}, and Borel C, P(B∩{Y_t∈C})=P(B)P_i(C) and E[Y_t 1_B]=μ_i P(B).
For integer n≥5, a>0 and L=log n, the sum over 1≤s<n of exp(−((a sqrt(s)−2 sqrt(L))_+)²/2) is at most 1+8L/a². For n≥12 it is at most 8L/a².
For n≥max{k,2}, centered 1-sub-Gaussian reward-stack entries and the stated UCB algorithm with δ=n⁻², every arm with Δ_i>0 satisfies E[T_i(n)]≤3+8 log(n)/Δ_i².
For n≥max{k,2}, 1-sub-Gaussian reward-stack entries and UCB with δ=n⁻², every arm with Δ_i>0 satisfies E[T_i(n)]≤3+16 log(n)/Δ_i².
